newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sugar trade attack export refund control plans.
newsitem.headline: EU sugar trade attack export refund control plans.

text.p: European sugar exporters attacked plans, intended to combat fraud, which would make export refunds dependent on proof of arrival and consumption in the country of destination.
"Our members believe that 40 percent of all EU sugar exports would be jeopardized if this planned regulation was applied," the European Sugar Trade Association (ASSUC) said in a statement.
Payment of the export refunds, which cover 60 percent of of the value of the sugar, would depend entirely on the goodwill of the buyer, it added.
It said that documents proving the arrival of sugar shipments would be difficult to obtain given that EU sugar is exported to more than 100 countries.

"The responsibility of the exporter should end when the goods have left the EU territory...," it said, adding it is up to customs authorities to impose import levies if sugar is re-imported into the EU.
Various European Commission departments are discussing a regulation covering export refunds for sugar, cereals, beef, dairy and other agricultural products.
ASSUC Secretary General Hannelore Mill said the impact on sugar exports, for which there is only a single refund, would be much greater than on other farm products.
The Commission is expected to present a draft text to the EU trade mechanisms committee in the next few weeks.
